text:
ops-bot: Alert — dedicated pool 'dedicated-east-6' GPU_utilization > 85% for 12m (alert_id: A-9821)
alex: saw the alert, looks like autoscaler didn't add nodes fast enough. queue length spiked.
maya: where's the per-pool grafana panel that shows scaling events + pending requests?
liam: Dashboard -> https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/pools/dedicated-pools?orgId=1&var-pool=dedicated-east-6 (top row has autoscale events and group-by node-type)
jess: can someone share the PromQL we use for sustained GPU util? want to propose a tweak to the threshold.
liam: sure, current expression we use for alerting:  
```
avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent{pool=\"dedicated-east-6\"}[12m]) > 0.85
```
liam: that's average across all GPUs in the pool — causes noise when one node is hot.
maya: proposal: change to p95 over 10m and require queue_length > 3 to avoid spike noise. e.g.
```
quantile_over_time(0.95, gpu_utilization_percent{pool=\"dedicated-east-6\"}[10m]) > 0.80 and avg_over_time(request_queue_length{pool=\"dedicated-east-6\"}[10m]) > 3
```
maya: rationale: we want to avoid firing for short transient hotspots but still catch sustained saturation that affects latency.
ajex: @alex (typo) — tagging @sre-oncall to confirm suppression windows for scheduled deploys.
sre-oncall: @maya +1 on using p95 + queue condition, but prefer 10m -> 15m window for stability. Also suggest adding a 'suppression' label during pool maintenance windows.
jess: can we also add a companion alert for "scale failures" — when desired_replicas > current_replicas for >5m? I've seen cases where autoscaler failed to provision a node.
liam: good call. example expression: 
```
(max(desired_replicas{pool=\"dedicated-east-6\"}) - max(current_replicas{pool=\"dedicated-east-6\"})) > 0 and increase(desired_replicas{pool=\"dedicated-east-6\"}[5m]) > 0
```
liam: that should surface when the control plane requested more but nodes never appeared.
alex: also adding log queries for postmortem: Loki snippet to find OOMs/evictions:
```
{app=\"inference\", pool=\"dedicated-east-6\"} |= \"evicted\" or |= \"OOM\" | json | line_format \"{{.msg}}\"
```
alex: helpful to correlate with GPU driver logs: /logs/gpu-node-exporter/* (linked in docs).
maya: can we get a small panel added to the pool overview: p50/p95 latency, queue length, pending deployments, and failures/evictions? even a compact 2x2 is enough.
liam: I can add a PR to grafana-dashboards repo with a new panel. will ping when ready.
jess: tagging infra: @alex please also open a short infra-runbook note: what to do when scale alert fires and scale failure alert both fire. quick steps (1-3) for oncall.
alex: will draft runbook and link to the dashboard PR.
ops-bot: Scheduled maintenance window for dedicated-east-6 tomorrow 02:00-03:00 UTC — suppress autoscale alerts during window.
sre-oncall: ack. will not change alert thresholds while suppression is active. After maintenance I'll run a 24h lookback to see if the new rule behaves.
maya: one more ask — can we make alert comments include a quick link to the most recent autoscaler logs for that pool? saves time during triage.
liam: yep, we can add template: https://logs.redwood.internal/?q=pool%3Ddedicated-east-6%20autoscaler and include in alert 'runbook_url' field.
jess: PR for alert change and new 'scale-failure' alert: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/alerts/pulls/412 — reviewers: @liam @sre-oncall
alex: quick review pass done, left tiny nits about labels.
sre-oncall: will approve once the suppression label is present.
oncall-bot: Deploy queued: infra-alerts v2.3 -> staging in 15m.
maya: thanks — once deployed let's watch the pool for an hour and collect p95 -> report back here.
liam: noted, monitoring for the next 60m. will post snapshots.
alex: thanks all, this should reduce noisy alerts and help with sustained saturation detection.
ops-bot: Alert resolved — GPU_utilization back to normal for dedicated-east-6
liam: posting graphs: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d-solo/snapshots/abc123 (p95 and queue snapshots)
maya: looks good, p95 down and queue drained. closing loop. :white_check_mark:
